binders: For every rate λ in NNReal, i.e. every nonnegative real rate including λ=0.
In the first conjunct, k is a natural-number index tending to infinity through Filter.atTop.
In the second conjunct, for every implicit natural number k.
hypotheses: The rate has the built-in subtype condition 0≤λ.
For the tail inequalities at a given k, assume λ<k after both are viewed as real numbers.
conclusions: The function pλ(k)=poissonPMFReal λ k is asymptotically equivalent as k→∞ to exp(-λ)·((e·λ)/k)^k/sqrt(2kπ). Concretely, the difference between pλ and this displayed function is little-o of the displayed function along atTop.
Whenever k is a natural number with λ<k, the point mass pλ(k) is at most the real-valued Poisson upper-tail mass of {n∈Nat | k≤n}, and that tail mass is at most exp(-λ)·((e·λ)/k)^k.
mathematical_definitions: pλ(k)=exp(-λ)·λ^k/k!, by the supplied definition of poissonPMFReal.
poissonMeasure λ is the measure on Nat induced by the Poisson probability mass function.
IsEquivalent at atTop means pλ-Aλ=o(Aλ) as the natural index tends to infinity.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every nonnegative real Poisson rate λ, the mass at the natural number k has the displayed Stirling-type asymptotic exp(-λ)((eλ)/k)^k/sqrt(2πk) as k tends to infinity. Moreover, for every natural k strictly larger than λ, the mass at k is no greater than the probability of the upper tail n≥k, and that upper tail is no greater than exp(-λ)((eλ)/k)^k.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The statement quantifies over λ=0 as well as positive rates; it imposes no positivity hypothesis on the rate.
At λ=0, both the Poisson mass and the comparison function are eventually zero, so the little-o formulation of equivalence can hold degenerately rather than expressing a nonzero ratio tending to one.
The tail assertion is an implication and therefore states nothing for natural k with k≤λ.
Because λ≥0 and λ<k, the tail-bound branch necessarily has k≥1, so the quotient by k in that branch avoids a zero denominator.

The asymptotic comparison function is nevertheless defined for every natural k, including k=0. Lean's real division, square root, and natural power are total operations, and atTop ignores finitely many initial values.
IsEquivalent is encoded as a little-o statement about the difference; the proposition does not separately assert eventual nonvanishing or a quotient limit.
The middle tail quantity uses Measure.real, namely toReal of an extended nonnegative measure value, rather than directly retaining an extended-real probability.
The event is written using inequalities between real casts of natural numbers; no separate natural-order reformulation is part of the proposition.
ambiguities: The supplied one-level definition of Real.pi says only that it is twice a chosen cosine zero; without the omitted specification of that existence theorem, the packet does not independently characterize which zero is chosen or establish the usual positive π constant.

The packet supplies only one-level boundaries for notions such as little-o, complex exponential, the underlying Poisson PMF-to-measure construction, and NNReal square root; their familiar mathematical interpretations are used above, but their deeper definitions are not present in the dossier.
